card.title: Free HTTPS, no DNS setup
card.description: Serve this dashboard and your apps over HTTPS with a real Let's Encrypt certificate. Nothing to configure at a registrar.
card.compactHint: Until it is on, addresses are plain http and not secure.
card.noPublicIp: This server's public IP address is not known, so a zero-DNS hostname cannot be built. Set APP_PUBLIC_HOST to the IP on the control plane and restart it, or use your own domain below.
card.httpSignInNote: After it is on, sign in over the https address.
card.emailHelp: Any inbox you read works. Certificates are free and renew on their own: Let's Encrypt only emails you if one is about to expire and could not renew.
card.stagingLabel: Test with Let's Encrypt staging first
card.stagingHelp: Staging certificates are not trusted by browsers, but it has no meaningful rate limits. Use it to prove ports 80 and 443 are reachable.
card.recheckHelp: If the address does not resolve to this server yet, fix it where the DNS or firewall is managed, then re-check. Nothing else needs to change here.
card.pending: Requesting a certificate for {{domain}}. This usually takes under a minute.
card.issuedDetail: Issued by {{issuer}}, expires {{date}}. Renewal is automatic.
card.stagingIssued: This is a staging certificate, so browsers will show a warning. Turn staging off and run it again to get a trusted one.
card.dashboardUrlFailed: Could not save the dashboard URL.
card.preflightBody: This server could not reach itself on port {{ports}} at its public address. Let's Encrypt must reach port 80 (and 443 for renewals) from the internet. Open them in your cloud firewall or run the firewall step in setup. This check can be wrong behind some routers, so wait for the certificate before changing anything.

hint.unreachable: Let's Encrypt could not reach this server on port 80. Open ports 80 and 443 in your firewall and your cloud provider's security group, then try again.
hint.rate_limited: Let's Encrypt is rate limiting this hostname. Wait before retrying, and use staging while you debug.
hint.dns: The hostname did not resolve to this server. Check that the detected public IP is correct.
hint.caa: A CAA DNS record forbids Let's Encrypt from issuing for this hostname.
hint.unknown: Let's Encrypt refused the request. The full response is below and in the control plane log.

fallback.title: Automatic app hostnames
fallback.description: Apps without a domain get https://<app>.<dashed-ip>.<provider> from a free wildcard-DNS service with automatic TLS, so a fresh deploy is reachable with zero DNS.
fallback.toggleLabel: Give apps without a domain an automatic hostname
fallback.noPublicHost: No public address detected. Set APP_PUBLIC_HOST on the control plane to turn this on.

dnsProvider.defaultLabel: Wildcard DNS provider (default for all apps)
dnsProvider.appLabel: Wildcard DNS provider for this app
dnsProvider.inheritNote: This app follows the provider chosen in Settings, Domains.
dnsProvider.customNote: Use your own wildcard record, so apps are named <app>.<your base domain>.
dnsProvider.baseHint: Point *.{{domain}} at this server with an A record, then run Test resolution.
dnsProvider.betaHint: Free public service. Fine for testing, not recommended for production traffic.
dnsProvider.saveFailed: Could not update the wildcard DNS provider.
dnsProvider.confirmBody: This app is currently reachable at {{host}}.
dnsProvider.confirmOldStops: The old hostname stops working as soon as the new one is routed.
dnsProvider.confirmNoDowntime: The route updates in place with no downtime. Bookmarks and webhooks using the old hostname need updating.

network.off: Automatic hostnames are turned off for this server.
network.noPublicHost: No public IP is known for this server, so no automatic hostname can be built. Set APP_PUBLIC_HOST on the control plane.

wizard.sslipReady: HTTPS is ready on the free hostname. You can continue, or set up your own domain too.

certTable.internalHint: Signed by this server's own short-lived CA and renewed automatically. Browsers show a warning until you enable HTTPS.
certTable.proxyRenews: Managed by your proxy, renews automatically.
certTable.proxyUnknown: Managed by your proxy. Not seen yet: verify the route on the proxy page.

domainCert.title: Get a real certificate for {{domain}}
domainCert.intro: This checks that {{domain}} points here and that Let's Encrypt can reach this server, then asks for a trusted certificate. Until then visitors see a browser warning.
domainCert.appliesToAll: Public certificates are a server setting: turning them on applies to every domain on this server, and renewals are automatic.
domainCert.checking: Checking DNS, port 80, CAA records, your contact email and Let's Encrypt limits
domainCert.emailHelp: Defaults to your admin account. Let's Encrypt only writes if a certificate is about to expire and could not renew.
domainCert.stagingLabel: Rehearse with Let's Encrypt staging first
domainCert.stagingHelp: Staging has no meaningful limits but signs with a test CA. Browsers will not trust the result, so run it again without staging afterwards.
domainCert.stagingWarning: Staging certificates are untrusted: visitors still see a warning.
domainCert.ackPorts: I know ports 80 and 443 are open (this server may not be able to reach itself)

progress.pendingBody: Let's Encrypt is checking that you control {{domain}}. This usually takes under a minute.
progress.failedTitle: Let's Encrypt did not issue the certificate
progress.stagingIssued: This is a staging certificate, so browsers still show a warning. Run this again without staging to get a trusted one.

kindHint.none: No certificate has been issued for this domain yet.
kindHint.internal: Signed by this server itself. Browsers do not trust it and show a warning.
kindHint.staging: Signed by the Let's Encrypt test CA. Browsers do not trust it.
kindHint.letsencrypt: Signed by Let's Encrypt and renewed automatically.
kindHint.custom: A certificate you uploaded. It does not renew itself.
kindHint.proxy: Issued and renewed by the proxy in front of this server.
kindHint.other: Signed by a public certificate authority.

portEditor.publishedPortsHint: HOST:CONTAINER/udp or /tcp, comma separated. Published on this server only.

errors.protocol: "{{entry}}": protocol must be tcp or udp
